title: Prefill-aware kernel confidence lattice and graceful fallback policy
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: implement a runtime component that builds a per-arch / per-seqlen ‘confidence lattice’ — a compact representation of kernel candidates ordered by expected latency/cost/accuracy confidence — and uses it to drive safe, observable kernel switches during prefill and decode.

Problem: current kernel picker picks options based on static heuristics and single-metric cost models. This leads to occasional latency SLO violations for mixed bursts (variable prefill lengths + short decodes) and suboptimal cost under shifting seqlen distributions. We need a confidence-aware policy that: (1) encodes uncertainty about microbenchmark estimates, (2) tracks online calibration drift, (3) defines explicit thresholds for graceful fallback cascades between kernel variants and quantization levels, and (4) supports staged rollout with telemetry-driven autotuning.

Approach:
- Build a lattice data structure keyed by (arch fingerprint, seqlen bucket, opvariant signature) that stores: estimated median latency, tail latency bound (p95/p99), cost proxy, recent calibration factor, and a confidence score derived from sample count + variance. The lattice is intentionally small (<=8 candidates per bucket) and prioritized by an objective function (latency SLO penalty + cost weight + confidence bonus).
- Prefill/Decode split: during prefill we bias toward kernels with stable tail behavior and high confidence; during decode we bias toward low median latency kernels but maintain a safety margin. The runtime will keep separate lattice entries for prefill-mode vs decode-mode for the same (arch,seqlen) bucket.
- Fallback policy: define a graceful cascade: preferred -> safe-hedge -> quantized-fallback -> diversified-retry. Each transition has backoff windows and rollback triggers based on telemetry (increased tail or error rate).
- Online autotune: collect lightweight microbench samples and request-level telemetry (latency histogram, error/class mismatch) to update lattice estimates. Use a conservative Bayesian update to adjust confidence and reweight candidates; only promote a new kernel after N sequential windows of stable improvement or via canary routes.
- Safety & observability: emit per-request decision tags (kernel_id, lattice_version, confidence) to tracing; add rollback rules into Console rollout manager (canary size, error thresholds). Include a simulator mode to run candidate selection on historical traces and produce projected SLO/cost deltas.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
1) P95 latency regressions vs baseline <= 3% for traffic flows in A/B tests (canary 5% traffic).
2) Median token cost reduction >= 6% for mixed workloads where lattice picks quantized fallbacks safely.
3) Laddered fallback rollbacks trigger correctly under synthetic tail-injection tests.
4) Lattice storage + decision time overhead <= 2% CPU and 1ms median decision latency added.

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Quantization fallback risks output quality drift; need integrated eval harness (quality delta per prompt set) before promoting quantized candidates.
- Per-tenant calibration vs global lattice: storing per-tenant lattices increases memory but improves personalization. Start global+region, evaluate per-tenant hot-paths later.
- Choosing confidence function (sample-count vs variance vs bootstrap) — initial plan uses a sample-count weighted variance-based score but we should prototype a Bayesian posterior predictive interval approach if time allows.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design lattice proto and wire-level tags (1 week).
2) Microbench harness extension to record seqlen-prefill/decode pairs and produce candidate summaries (2 weeks).
3) Runtime integration: lightweight lattice cache, selection policy, and fallback state machine (3 weeks).
4) Telemetry and Console dashboard: per-lattice metric surfaces and rollout controls (2 weeks parallel).
5) Canary + synthetic tail tests + rollout (2 weeks).

Rollout plan: start with internal canary on staging, then 2% production traffic in controlled customer group, then step up to 20% with automatic rollback rules. Autotune will initially only recommend promotions; full automatic promotions after 2 months of stable telemetry.
